about: What makes a skill good as a system prompt, as checks the lab can run (node lab.mjs skill grade). Each criterion scores 0-2; `portable` ones apply to any skill collection (they also grade the reference repositories, so ours is compared with theirs), `lab` ones need this repository (commands, rules, routing). `fix` is what the refine brief tells the AI; `source` is where the criterion comes from. The rubric is itself know-how: a criterion that does not predict bench results (skill growth: rubric validity) is rewritten or retired, like a rule. History: v1 (14 criteria) saturated at a mean of 96% after the first refine round; v2 added no-repeat. v3 (2026-10-03): rules-why gives 2 when a skill has no hard rule (v1-2 gave 1, and an AI asked to raise it invented "(when missed: …)" consequences); evidence is marked text:false (only a probe or a test raises it, never an edit).

criteria.what: name is kebab-case, at most 64 characters, the same as its folder
criteria.fix: rename the folder or the `name:` line so they match (lowercase words joined by -)
criteria.source: OpenAI skill-creator quick_validate; boredape874/mcbejsonuimasterAI tools/skill-lint.mjs (NAME_MISMATCH, NAME_INVALID)

criteria.what: the description says what it does in its first sentence and when to use it (Use when / for / after / first), in at most 500 characters
criteria.fix: description: first sentence = what it does (with the words a person would say); then `Use when ...` with 2-4 concrete triggers (file names, symptoms, request words); cut it under 500 characters: hosts shorten long descriptions and match on the front
criteria.source: Codex skills docs (front-load the use case and trigger words; descriptions are shortened first); Anthropic skill authoring best practices (what it does + when to use it)

criteria.what: says when NOT to use it and which skill takes that work instead
criteria.fix: add one line: `Not for X (use `other-skill`)`; a skill that knows its edge stops the AI from loading two that overlap
criteria.source: Codex skills docs (when it should and should not trigger); mcbejsonuimasterAI mcbe-json-ui-master (one primary owner, hand-offs by name)

criteria.what: numbered steps (at least 3), each an action
criteria.fix: turn the advice into numbered steps that start with a verb or a command, in the order the work happens
criteria.source: SkillsBench arXiv 2602.12670 (procedural, stepwise guidance helps; declarative documentation much less)

criteria.what: at least one concrete, working example: a command with its arguments, a code block, or e.g.
criteria.fix: add a real command line with real arguments (one that works in this repository), or one short code block
criteria.source: SkillsBench arXiv 2602.12670 (concise guidance with at least one working example beats exhaustive documentation)

criteria.what: its hard rules (never / always / must / only) say what goes wrong when they are missed; a skill with no hard rule has nothing to explain (2)
criteria.fix: give each hard rule its consequence (`... (when missed: <symptom>)`); a rule with its symptom is followed and recognised; in this lab put rules in skills/knowledge.json with `why`
criteria.source: iMasterProX/mcbemodelingmasterAI (every rule is a past failure); bds-lab knowledge.json

criteria.what: says what done looks like and what to report
criteria.fix: end with `Done when <what proves it>. Report: <what ran, what passed, what is not verified>`
criteria.source: mcbejsonuimasterAI route contract (Input / Output / Success); mcbemodelingmasterAI mcbe-model-verification

criteria.what: says what it cannot prove and asks to say so instead of claiming it
criteria.fix: name the limit (static check, render, sandbox) and the sentence to use: `say what was not verified`
criteria.source: mcbemodelingmasterAI (if you have not rendered it or run it, say so); mcbejsonuimasterAI docs/22 (confirmed / inferred / not verified labels)

criteria.what: 500 to 3200 bytes: read whole, every turn, so small; not so small it says nothing
criteria.fix: over: move detail behind a command (`help <topic>`, `skill <other>`) or retire rules that never fire; under: add the procedure and an example
criteria.source: SkillsBench arXiv 2602.12670 (compact and detailed skills help; comprehensive ones hurt: -2.9pp); Codex skills docs (skill list capped at 2% of context / 8,000 characters)

criteria.what: no AI-product-specific tool names, absolute paths or backslash paths in SKILL.md (those go in skills/<name>/ai/<ai>.md)
criteria.fix: write the step as a plain command or file action any AI can do; move what only one AI needs to skills/<name>/ai/<claude|codex|gemini|cursor|copilot>.md (skill install adds it for that AI only)
criteria.source: the request for skills every AI can use; mcbejsonuimasterAI skill-lint (NON_PORTABLE_REFERENCE)

criteria.what: one job: it does not repeat a sibling skill (word overlap under 30%)
criteria.fix: move the shared part to one skill and point at it by name; SkillsBench: 2-3 focused skills per task beat 4+

criteria.what: does not say again what the always-loaded entry file (AGENTS.md) already says
criteria.fix: cut the lines the grade quotes (the AI has read AGENTS.md already) or point at it in a few words; what the skill adds is the part AGENTS.md does not say
criteria.source: rubric v2, added when v1 saturated (mean 96%): bds-lab docs/TOKENS (every line read every turn costs tokens); Lost in the Middle arXiv 2307.03172 (repeated, long context dilutes what matters)

criteria.what: every command and repository path it names exists here
criteria.fix: fix or remove the command / path the grade names (`help <word>` finds the real one)
criteria.source: mcbejsonuimasterAI skill-lint (REFERENCE_MISSING) and skill-doctor (never invoke a tool that is absent)

criteria.what: its rules can be re-run here (test / probe / unit), not only seen once or quoted
criteria.fix: write a probe (skills/probes/<id>: addon + tests.txt) or point a rule at a test, then skill promote <id> --evidence probe:...
criteria.source: bds-lab (rules re-checked on the real server after each Minecraft update)

criteria.what: the router finds it: bds-addon-master names it, and `skill route` puts it first for the requests it owns (skills/routes.json)
criteria.fix: name it in bds-addon-master; put the words people use (any language) in skills/<name>/triggers.txt and the description; `skill route "<request>"` shows what wins and why
criteria.source: mcbejsonuimasterAI tests/skill-routing-and-sync.mjs (routing tested); Codex skills docs (implicit invocation matches the description)
